question: Drug of choice for neurogenic diabetes insipidus
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Neurogenic diabetes insipidus" -> "deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (ADH)" -> "Desmopressin mimics ADH" -> "reduces urine output and increases urine osmolality" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Neurogenic diabetes insipidus" -> "results in excessive urination and thirst due to ADH deficiency" -> "Desmopressin replaces missing ADH" -> "restores normal fluid balance" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Neurogenic diabetes insipidus" -> "ADH not properly produced or released" -> "Desmopressin provides ADH activity" -> "decreases urine production and increases concentration" -> 95%
analysis: Desmopressin is the drug of choice for neurogenic diabetes insipidus because it effectively replaces the deficient ADH, thereby managing the symptoms of excessive urination and thirst. It is preferred for its efficacy and safety profile.
